sources.entry: Cython - Optimizing static compiler for Python.

summary.one_liner: Cython is an optimising static compiler that translates Python code (plus optional C-style type declarations) into C/C++ extension code.
summary.what_it_does: Translates Python code to C or C++ and can call C functions and declare C types on variables and class attributes. Developers can tune code from broad to fine-grained levels so the generated C code runs efficiently. It is described as well suited for wrapping external C libraries and for writing fast C modules that speed up Python code. Installation is via pip install Cython when a C compiler is already available. The README contrasts it with PyPy, Numba, Pythran, mypyc and Nuitka, and claims it supports full runtime compatibility with CPython versions and other C-API implementations such as PyPy and Pyston. It also notes its origins in Greg Ewing's Pyrex.
use_cases: speed up slow Python code with C extensions
wrap external C or C++ libraries for Python
write fast native modules for CPython
add static type declarations to Python for optimisation
notable: Generates C/C++ from Python, with optional C type declarations for manual tuning
Can call C functions directly and wrap C/C++ libraries
Based on Pyrex, with more than two decades of development
Supports PyPy and Pyston C-API implementations according to the README
caveats: Requires a C compiler for installation, otherwise the README points to a separate installation page
README does not state specific platform limits
